sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by live-cell STED imaging of Halo-tagged CD45 at the plasma membrane in Jurkat T cells; no phosphatase activity or signalling assay reported in these clips.
sites.rationale: PTPRC has exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 26 (Q) after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 25 (G); the C-terminus (residue 1306) is intracellular. Because L3/L4 report a surface-displayed endogenous Halo-tagged CD45 but name no residue, topology_derived applies and the junction is uniquely determined as insert_after_residue=25. Python confirms seq[24]='G' and seq[25]='Q', placing the tag 552 residues from the TM boundary (578), well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. L4 confirms extracellular accessibility by live-cell STED. Halo tag knocked in at the endogenous PTPRC locus in Jurkat T cells (L3), creating a full-length surface-displayed CD45-Halo fusion confirmed by live-cell STED imaging at the plasma membrane (L4). No residue number is stated in either clip.

sources.claim: To avoid artefacts generated by protein overexpression, we knocked in a Halo tag at the endogenous loci of ZAP-70, Lck, LAT or CD45 in Jurkat T cells (Fig. 1A ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 describe an HA-CD45 chimeric construct in which the HA tag is inserted into the N-terminus of mouse LAT (after its starting methionine); CD45 contributes only its cytoplasmic domain (residues 598–1304) to this chimera. The HA tag therefore resides in LAT's extracellular portion, not in CD45's extracellular domain. This construct does not constitute a tag insertion in CD45's ECD and was excluded from sites. No residue number is given for the Halo-tag knock-in in L3/L4, so the position is topology-derived rather than validated. Confidence is medium because the exact junction within the endogenous locus is not disclosed in the ledger clips.
